subject: phoenix
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: phoenix with flame plumage, wings spread.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I'm looking at the rendered wings and noticing the arms read as plain thin red bars, with feathers lying flat in the horizontal plane so they appear as thin edge-on slivers rather than visible shapes from the front — they're too narrow to register properly.

I want to widen and thicken the feathers so the wing reads as a continuous surface, and reconsider spacing so overlaps don't just create stripes. The body also looks too small compared to the wings, like a tiny chicken on stilts, so I should scale up its radii to make it rounder and more proportionate, while keeping legs and feet roughly as they are since those read fine in the side view.

The wing arm tube is showing through as a bare red bar, so I'll thicken the coverts and scatter small fluff cards along the arm sweep to hide it better, plus lift the arm's color toward flame tones. Flame cards at the wingtips look fine, but the tail ribbons are too flat and read as thin lines edge-on in the side view since they're lying in a horizontal plane -- I need to rework their orientation so the fan reads properly from the side.

I'll also scale up the head slightly by enlarging the skull and eye decals since they look small, and double-check the foot placement against the dais height so the toes don't appear to sink into the ground.

Skipping ink outlines for now given time constraints. Final edit list: enlarge body and head with bigger eyes, add fluff cards and wider coverts to the wing arm, and widen the primary and secondary feathers for a fuller plumage look.

Still adjusting proportions...

I'm also checking that the neck, collar, and ring radii nest properly against the larger body so nothing gets buried, tweaking values like neck to 0.2/0.13/0.1 and collar to 0.19 to keep clearances sensible, then moving to update the arm sweep thickness profile.

Switching to the card hits and flow direction, I set flow to [0,-0.2,-1] with a 60-degree lean and size range [0.07,0.16], filtering so only cards with y greater than -0.2 show, and confirm hit-carried bones are fine. I also adjust the body sweep radii profile for a fuller thigh-to-shoulder taper, and finalize unique skull scale and eye size values.
